provisions.summary: Renewable energy technologies income tax credit: adds AGI limits ($175,000 individual, $350,000 joint), an aggregate annual cap of $40,000,000 for 2027-2030, and ends the credit for taxable years after 2029. The credit is not modeled.
provisions.quote: This section shall not apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2029.

provisions.summary: Replaces the scheduled 2027 and 2029 bracket steps with new schedules: 2.5% and 5.0% rates in the second and third brackets, and a new 13% top rate. The 2029 schedule shifts the brackets again.
Capital goods excise tax credit sunsets after tax year 2027. The spec cannot express business credits.
provisions.quote: This section shall not apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2027.

provisions.summary: Renewable fuels production tax credit sunsets after tax year 2028. The spec cannot express industry credits.
provisions.quote: This section shall not apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2028.

provisions.summary: Repeals the high technology business investment tax credit effective January 1, 2029. The spec cannot express industry credits.
provisions.quote: Section 235-110.9, Hawaii Revised Statutes, is repealed.

provisions.summary: Repeals the technology infrastructure renovation tax credit effective January 1, 2028. The spec cannot express industry credits.
provisions.quote: Section 235-110.51, Hawaii Revised Statutes, is repealed.

provisions.summary: Moves the effective date of Part II of Act 261, SLH 2019 (the tax credit for research activities repeal) from January 1, 2030 to January 1, 2029. The spec cannot express industry credits.
provisions.quote: Part II shall take effect on [January 1, 2030.] January 1, 2029.

notes: The bill repeals the bracketed 2027 and 2029 schedules from the earlier law and replaces them with new schedules for 2027 and 2029. The 2029 schedule stays in force through 2031, so the spec has two vintages. Married filing separately uses the single schedule, as the model does by default. The bill does not touch the standard deduction, personal exemption, capital gains alternative tax, EITC or food/excise credit, so those keys are omitted and current law (Act 24) applies. Section 1's AGI limits apply to tax years after 2026, and its aggregate cap and sunset take effect from 2027 and after 2029 respectively; none of these can be modeled. Sections 8 and 9 are boilerplate and effective-date provisions. Section 9 makes sections 2, 3 and 4 apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2026 (section 3's credit ends after 2027 and section 4's after 2028 through their own sunset clauses), section 6 effective January 1, 2028, and section 5 effective January 1, 2029.
